chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from someone who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said in a speech of his: 'Whoever extends his hand with kindness when he finds the means, Allah will replace for him what he spent in his world, and multiply it for him in his Hereafter.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for spending in the way of Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the concept of *Istibdal* (divine substitution) where Allah replaces spent wealth with something better, a principle deeply rooted in Shia theological discourse on economic justice. It underscores the dual benefit of charity: immediate material restoration in this world and exponential spiritual multiplication in the Hereafter, reflecting the Imam's role in elucidating the practical applications of Quranic teachings.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from someone who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said in a speech of his<sup>asws</sup>: ‘The one who extends his (helping) hand with the act of kindness and when he bears it (the expenditure), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Replace for him what he had spent in his world, and would Double it, for him, in his Hereafter’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthaman ibn ‘Isa from certain individuals who narrated to him who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, in one of his speeches, ‘
If one extends his hand to provide Benevolent Assistance when he is able to do so, Allah replaces, in this world, what he has spent and will grant them double reward in the next life.’”
